author: current Codex assistant
reasoning: For a proposed gathering vertex, each incident branch has workload equal to the sum of distances of its pieces to that vertex. A move between different branches removes one unit from each; a move confined to one branch, including a root piece entering it, leaves that branch workload unchanged. Therefore total workload must be even and no branch may exceed the sum of the others. These conditions suffice by repeatedly pairing pieces from the two largest remaining branches and moving them toward the root. Each operation reduces total distance by2, attaining the distance lower bound. Rerooted subtree counts and distance sums test all possible gathering vertices in linear time.
